status: Initial food and environment proposals for review

variants.title: Ingredients & prepared states
variants.summary: Tomato, cucumber, carrot and mushroom—whole and chopped.
variants.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: Bara Kitchen food and environment concept art for a cute 3D cooking game.
Input image 1 is the APPROVED CHARACTER STYLE reference. Match its soft rounded 3D game rendering, friendly oversized simple shapes, broad readable colors and gently matte surfaces. It is not an object to copy into this sheet: NO characters, faces or eyes on the food or furniture.
Shared café materials: light honey-oak wood, muted sage-green painted cabinet fronts, warm ivory countertops/ceramics, cocoa-brown details, understated brushed-silver metal. Food uses richer red/orange/green/cream so it stands out from the calm environment. Large soft bevels, short chunky proportions, simple geometric construction. No sharp low-poly facets, grime-heavy realism, ornate decoration, noisy material texture or tiny functional details.
Presentation: a professional asset concept sheet on a warm ivory background, isolated objects with soft grounding shadows, a consistent slightly elevated three-quarter camera so tops and fronts are visible. Clean dark cocoa sans-serif labels, restrained generous spacing. No perspective room background, no UI meters or code, no logos/watermark. The labels describe assets and are outside the objects.

Create an eight-cell SQUARE sheet arranged in FOUR ROWS and TWO COLUMNS. Row order: tomato, cucumber, carrot, mushroom. LEFT column is WHOLE, RIGHT column is CHOPPED. Put small column headings "WHOLE" and "CHOPPED", and a species name beside each row. Exactly these four food ingredients, no extra foods or garnish.
Row 1 TOMATO: one squat plump red tomato with a small thick five-point green stem; opposite, a compact pile of exactly FOUR generous tomato wedges showing brighter interior and a few simple pale seed pockets. No green stem mixed into chopped food.
Row 2 CUCUMBER: one short thick slightly curved dark-green cucumber, subtle broad highlights rather than tiny bumps; opposite, FIVE thick green-edged pale-green cucumber coins with a simple three-seed motif.
Row 3 CARROT: one short stout orange carrot, blunt taper and a small attached green top; opposite, FIVE large orange half-round chunks, no green leaves in the prepared pile.
Row 4 MUSHROOM: one friendly edible cream-and-warm-taupe button mushroom with broad domed cap and thick short stem, NO red cap or spots; opposite, FOUR thick recognizable mushroom slices, each preserving the cap-and-stem outline and taupe cap edge.
All chopped piles are compact held-item-sized clusters, not heaps of dozens of tiny pieces. Whole and chopped versions retain the same palette and species identity. Make each raw ingredient readable at a small gameplay size. No plates, chopping boards, hands or kitchen props in this sheet.

variants.summary: Two recipes, with matching clean and dirty plate/bowl states.
variants.prompt:

Clean dark cocoa sans-serif labels, restrained generous spacing. No perspective room background, no UI meters or code, no logos/watermark. The labels describe assets and are outside the objects.

Create a SQUARE sheet of SIX cells, TWO ROWS by THREE COLUMNS. Top row is the same shallow round ceramic plate in three states. Bottom row is the same deep round ceramic soup bowl in three states. Ivory ceramics with a thick smooth rounded rim and one simple deep-teal rim stripe. The plate is flat and wide; the bowl is clearly deeper, with a small foot ring. Keep their relative scale consistent across each row.
Top-left label "CLEAN PLATE": an empty clean plate.
Top-center label "TOMATO–CUCUMBER SALAD": the same plate filled ONLY with generous red tomato wedges and thick dark-green-rimmed cucumber coins with pale-green centers. About four wedges and five coins, appetizing arranged but simple. Absolutely NO lettuce, herbs, cheese, dressing garnish, bread, or extra ingredients.
Top-right label "DIRTY PLATE": the identical plate empty except for broad muted sauce streaks and a few soft vegetable residue marks, no complete serving left. Clear dirty state without disgusting detail.
Bottom-left label "CLEAN BOWL": empty ivory soup bowl, pale-teal rim.
Bottom-center label "CARROT–MUSHROOM SOUP": same bowl containing warm golden-orange broth with several visible orange carrot chunks and four cream/taupe mushroom slices. NO parsley, herbs, noodles, croutons or extra ingredients. A little subtle steam may suggest warmth; do not hide the ingredients. Broth is recipe presentation, not another modeled pickup.
Bottom-right label "DIRTY BOWL": the same empty bowl with a visible ochre soup tide mark inside and one small residue patch.
No utensils, customers, food faces or additional dishes. Make clean/served/dirty silhouettes and contents easy to compare.

Create a SQUARE sheet of SIX clearly separated cells, TWO ROWS by THREE COLUMNS, full objects visible with these labels:
Top left "CHOPPING BOARD": a thick honey-oak rounded-rectangle board, shallow dark edge groove, a short stubby handle with a hanging hole; sturdy easy-to-model shape, no food on top.
Top middle "CHEF KNIFE": a chunky small kitchen knife with a broad short brushed-silver blade and an oversized navy handle, soft stylized edges, a simple single piece handle sized for a fingerless animal paw.
Top right "SOUP POT": a squat muted-sage enamel stockpot, cream rim, two short thick cocoa side handles, dark interior; matching domed lid placed beside it, knob large enough for a mitten paw. No soup in this study.
Bottom left "LADLE": a simple deep round brushed-silver spoon bowl with a short thick navy handle sized for the capybara; no long delicate shaft.
Bottom middle "WASHING TOOLS": one plump yellow sponge with a sage scrub surface and one small wooden dish brush with a short rounded handle; arranged as a single related pair.
Bottom right "DRYING RACK": a low honey-oak/cream rack with broad simple slots holding two clean ivory plates with teal rim stripes and one matching bowl, plus a small matte-metal drip tray.
Objects have practical relative sizes: board a little wider than a dinner plate, knife shorter than board width, pot diameter similar to a soup bowl but larger. Exaggerate handles and rims for readability, avoid micro-details. No extra utensils, knives in hands, food or room environment.

variants.summary: Prep, cooking, washing, serving, dish return and disposal.
variants.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: Bara Kitchen food and environment concept art for a cute 3D cooking game.
Input image 1 is the APPROVED CHARACTER STYLE reference. Match its soft rounded 3D game rendering, friendly oversized simple shapes, broad readable colors and gently matte surfaces. It is not an object to copy into this sheet: NO characters, faces or eyes on the food or furniture.

Presentation: a professional asset concept sheet on a warm ivory background, isolated objects with soft grounding shadows, a consistent slightly elevated three-quarter camera so tops and fronts are visible. Clean dark cocoa sans-serif labels, restrained generous spacing. No perspective room background, no UI meters or code, no logos/watermark. The labels describe assets and are outside the objects.

Create a SQUARE sheet with SIX isolated station concepts in TWO ROWS by THREE COLUMNS. Keep a consistent module scale and camera, all tops visible. Station design family is sage cabinet fronts, honey-oak worktops with generous rounded edges, ivory trim and cocoa handles. Most stations are one module wide; the dish conveyor may be two modules long. Stations are squat and low, designed so the approved chef's round head remains above the worktop.
Top left "PREP STATION": a low one-module cabinet with a thick rounded honey-oak top, a large light-wood chopping board positioned near the front interaction edge, and a navy-handled short chef knife resting safely on the board. Drawer with one wide simple handle. The board must be the obvious focal point.
Top middle "COOKING STATION": a matching single-module compact stovetop unit with two big simple dark burner circles and large brass/cocoa front control knobs; a squat sage enamel two-handled soup pot on one burner. Below is a cabinet panel, not a new baking recipe. No flame tower, fire or smoke hiding the pot.
Top right "WASHING STATION": a matching low unit with one large rounded brushed-silver sink basin, a thick curved ivory/metal tap and a clearly separate small side draining surface with a yellow sponge. Water basin plainly visible from above.
Bottom left "SERVING PASS": matching cabinet with an extra-wide uncluttered ivory pass surface, a broad deep-teal edge strip, a small brass service bell at the far corner and space for a plate and a bowl. No tall arch or canopy to obscure the chef; do not put a meal on it.
Bottom middle "DIRTY DISH RETURN": short low blue-gray conveyor belt with rounded end rollers, a honey-oak rim and two clear dirty dishes riding on top. One broad directional chevron on the belt. It has only the footprint of two counters, not a factory. This is a proposed dish-return prop; no customers in the sheet.
Bottom right "WASTE BIN": a short free-standing terracotta-red bin with a broad round dark opening in the top and an obvious simple cocoa trash-bin symbol on the front; rounded corners and a removable thick rim. Visually distinct from open wooden ingredient crates.
No ingredient storage crates, restaurant furniture, characters or UI. Keep all six useful interactions visually different and uncluttered.

Create a SQUARE sheet of SIX isolated supply modules, TWO ROWS by THREE COLUMNS, using exactly the same squat sage cabinet base, low honey-oak top/rim and ivory trim. Create a SQUARE sheet of SIX isolated modular café object families, TWO ROWS by THREE COLUMNS. Top surfaces visible. Keep the architecture and furniture low, chunky, rounded and modular; no giant room, no characters, no food. Same muted sage, honey oak, cream, cocoa and small navy accents as the kitchen.
Top left "COUNTER MODULES": a plain straight single-module sage cabinet with a rounded honey-oak worktop, and a matching L-shaped corner module beside it. Same low height, broad handles, no sink, stove or chopping board.
Top middle "FLOOR + WALL KIT": a small square patch of broad warm-cream and pale-clay checker tiles with very subtle grout; beside it, one simple cream plaster wall segment with honey-oak baseboard and a low sage wainscot strip. Show clean reusable module ends. Not a whole room.
Top right "TABLE + CHAIRS": one small round honey-oak café table on a stout pedestal with TWO low wooden chairs, soft rounded backrests and navy seat pads. Dining tabletop approximately the same low height as kitchen counters. No cutlery, plates or table decor.
Bottom left "BENCH + DIVIDER": one compact two-seat bench with sage upholstered cushion and honey-oak base, plus one separate low rounded honey-oak divider panel; these are a reusable seating/room separation family.
Bottom middle "WINDOW + PLANTER": a low cream wall module with a broad rounded-corner window in a honey-oak frame, a simple sage-striped fabric café awning, and a small terracotta planter with just three large simple rounded green leaves. No complex flowers, vines or fine leaves.
Bottom right "ENTRANCE + MENU": a simple honey-oak café door in a cream frame with a rounded rectangular glass pane and large cocoa handle, accompanied by a low rounded wooden menu stand with a plain dark slate board and two simple plate/bowl symbols—no legible long menu text.
Keep the silhouettes related to the approved soft character style. No detailed exterior streets, clutter, tiny ornamental furnishings, logos or faces on objects.
